description: Ex-SAAF medium transport helicopter. Confirmed on site by dated photographs of 22 November 2005 and 11 February 2007.

description: Complete ex-SAAF airframe. Dated photographs at the museum 6 March 2008. Designation contested: the SAAF list writes SE 316B, a malformed hybrid of two real marks; ABPic catalogues this airframe SE.3160. SA 316B is recorded because the SAAF list is internally consistent in giving the whole 600-serial block the B model while giving early serials the SE 3160. Not settled by photographic evidence.
museum_name: South African Air Force Museum Port Elizabeth

description: Ex-SAAF interceptor, the first Mirage F1CZ delivered to South Africa. Confirmed by a dated Wikimedia Commons photograph of 22 November 2005 explicitly captioned Mirage F1CZ reeksnommer 201.
museum_name: South African Air Force Museum Port Elizabeth

description: Ex-Fort Beaufort Military Museum. Variant corrected from FB.52 to FB.5: the SAAF Vampire FB5 batch was serialled 201 to 210 and 205 falls inside it, while the FB52 export batch is a later block, and ABPic captions a dated photograph of 11 February 2007 at the museum as a DH.100 Vampire FB5.

description: Single-seat ground-attack Impala. Confirmed on site by dated photographs of 22 November 2005 and 11 February 2007.

description: Ex-Silver Falcons display-team aircraft. Stood as an ACSA gate guard on a plinth at Port Elizabeth Airport, photographed there in 2001, 6 March 2008 and 7 November 2011, until it was taken down and moved across the airfield into the SAAF Museum branch on 7 May 2022 together with the Albatross, both badly corroded by the coastal climate. A future Friends of the SAAF Museum restoration project needing a replacement canopy, fuselage repair, undercarriage work and a full respray. Originally in the orange white and blue team scheme, later repainted overall silver, so its paint is not evidence of team identity.
aliases: Impala Mk I;Impala Mk 1;Impala Mk1;Atlas Impala;Aermacchi MB-326M;Aermacchi MB326M;Silver Falcons
museum_name: South African Air Force Museum Port Elizabeth

description: SAAF maritime patrol Albatross, a composite airframe built up with the wings of 888 by Classic Aircraft Maintenance and carrying the civil marks ZU-ABV rather than a SAAF serial. Stood as an airport gate guard, photographed there 6 March 2008 and 7 November 2011, and was moved into the SAAF Museum branch on 7 May 2022 alongside Impala 507. Heavily corroded on arrival.
museum_name: South African Air Force Museum Port Elizabeth

description: Ex-SAAF Harvard, confirmed on site by dated photographs in 2001, 22 November 2005, 1 December 2006 and 11 February 2007. Variant left blank: the SAAF list calls it an AT-6C Harvard Mk 4 while ABPic catalogues it as a Harvard IIA, and the conflict is unresolved. Not to be confused with Harvard 7480 which was on this site until at least 2007 and is now the airworthy ZU-DML at Swartkop.
museum_name: South African Air Force Museum Port Elizabeth

description: Ex-British Army Sioux AH.1, serial XT562, later on the South African civil register as ZS-HHA. Recorded at the museum from the 2005 to 2011 photographic surveys.
museum_name: South African Air Force Museum Port Elizabeth

description: Ex-Bahrain State Police Westland Scout, carrying the code GT rather than a serial. No serial has been established for this airframe so tail_number is deliberately blank. Photographed on site 22 November 2005, 1 December 2006 and 24 February 2011. Wikipedia describes a Wasp at this museum citing an archived 2013 page; the dated photographs and the SAAF list both say Scout.
museum_name: South African Air Force Museum Port Elizabeth

description: REPLICA, not a genuine airframe: a full-size wooden model, catalogued by ABPic on 24 February 2011 as Supermarine Spitfire IX (Replica) under the replica-register number BAPC.519, and described by Wikipedia as a 1:1 scale model built out of wood. Tail number deliberately blank because it has no airframe identity. Not to be confused with the museum organisation genuine Spitfire LF Mk IXe 5553 under long-term restoration at Swartkop.
museum_name: South African Air Force Museum Port Elizabeth

description: Jorg IV Skimmerfoil ground-effect craft, a wing-in-ground-effect vehicle rather than a conventional aeroplane, and one of the more unusual exhibits at the museum. Confirmed by a dated geotagged Wikimedia Commons photograph of 20 September 2007 taken on the museum site. Recorded as fixed_wing because it has fixed wings; no serial exists.
museum_name: South African Air Force Museum Port Elizabeth
